real_s3.explanation: The unit responds to a clearly visible, medium-sized vehicle wheel sitting inside its wheel arch, seen from the side or at an angle, most strongly a front wheel. It fires across vehicle types (cars, vans, buses, trucks).

parsed.explanation: The unit responds to a clearly visible, medium-sized vehicle wheel sitting inside its wheel arch, seen from the side or at an angle, most strongly a front wheel. It fires across vehicle types (cars, vans, buses, trucks).
parsed.evidence: Clearly visible wheels give d +1.38, while small or partly hidden wheels give d -1.10 and no wheel gives d -1.42, all at the extreme percentiles. Wheels inside an arch (+0.86), front wheels (+0.56), angled or side views (+0.67/+0.28) and medium wheel size (+1.10) are favored, while front/rear views where the wheel looks narrow (-1.09) and small far-away wheels (-0.97) are disfavored; vehicle type matters little (car -0.07, van +0.51, bus/truck +0.21).
parsed.missing_data: Photos of isolated wheels and arches outside the top vehicle classes (e.g., a detached tire, or a wheel arch with no tire), plus rear-wheel close-ups, to check whether the arch and the front position are needed or just correlated.

null_s1.explanation: The unit responds to large road vehicles (vans, buses, trucks, cars) seen side-on and level, so their wheels look round and fully visible. The fender or arch around the wheel is not what drives it.

parsed.explanation: The unit responds to large road vehicles (vans, buses, trucks, cars) seen side-on and level, so their wheels look round and fully visible. The fender or arch around the wheel is not what drives it.
parsed.evidence: Within its top classes, side views with round wheels (d +0.36, 96th pct) and level framing (d +0.57, 96th pct) raise activity, while front or rear views (d -0.84, 1st pct), small or partly hidden wheels (d -0.60, 1st pct) and tilted framing (d -0.57) lower it. The arch question barely separates photos (54th pct).
parsed.missing_data: Two things would most change this answer: the unit's response to side-view vehicles outside its top classes, and to rotated or flipped images. It would also help to see what the 9 no-wheel photos that still activate it (d +0.42) show.

parsed.explanation: The unit responds to a road vehicle seen side-on and level, with its wheel clearly visible and looking round. The wheel arch/fender part of the original description is not supported, and the upright-orientation claim could not be tested.
parsed.evidence: Within classes, side-view round wheels raise activity (d +0.36, pct 96), while front/rear views with narrow wheels (d -0.84, pct 1), small or partly hidden wheels (d -0.60, pct 1) and tilted horizons (d -0.57, pct 4) lower it. parsed.missing_data: Controlled edits: rotate the same vehicle from side to front view, remove or mask the wheel arch, and tilt or overturn the vehicle. Also a look at what the high-activity no-wheel photos contain.
